lines.japanese: その後、知ってる店をいくつか回って営業をかけてみたものの、残念ながら色良い返事はもらえなかった。
lines.english: After that, I made the rounds of a few places I knew and put out feelers for work. Unfortunately, nobody had anything for me.

lines.japanese: ２１時ちょい過ぎ。ピンフ通りに戻ってきた俺は、華々しいネオンといかがわしい働き蜂に囲まれてひとり、職にあぶれていた。
lines.english: A little past nine. Back on Pinfu Street, alone amid the gorgeous neon and disreputable worker bees, I remained out of a job.

lines.japanese: ランプポストの柱にケツを預けて小休止。
lines.english: I parked my ass against a lamppost and took a breather.

lines.japanese: 金はなくても歓楽街のマンウォッチングはそれなりに楽しい。なんたって、ちょっと首を左右に振るだけでいろんな人種が観察できる。
lines.english: Even without money, people-watching in the entertainment district offered its share of amusement. One turn of the head showed you every species of human being.

lines.japanese: やたらと道幅を占領して歩く大学生の一団。黒塗りの３ナンバーから降りてきた恰幅のいい男。防犯カメラの死角に立ちんぼしてるナイトメイクの女。
lines.english: A pack of college kids taking up far too much of the street. A portly man climbing out of a black luxury sedan. A heavily made-up woman soliciting in a security camera's blind spot.

lines.japanese: 夜行性の人間たちはよく誘蛾灯に群がる羽虫に喩えられたりするけど、それは言いえて妙だと思う。きっとみんな夜の太陽が大好きなんだ。
lines.english: Nocturnal people were often likened to winged insects swarming a bug lamp, and the comparison struck me as apt. Everyone must love the sun of the night.

lines.japanese: この時間になると、雑踏の中にはスーツ姿のお父さんも増えていた。お仕事お疲れさま。柳木原は夜たけなわだ。
lines.english: By this hour the crowd was filling with fathers in business suits. Another hard day's work. Yanagihara was in full nocturnal bloom.

lines.japanese: そのとき俺はもの欲しそうな顔でもしてたのだろうか。出るとこ出てるえっちな体をファー付きの真っ白いコートに包んだ、アジア系の若い女が近付いてくる。
lines.english: Maybe I looked hungry. A young Asian woman approached in a snow-white fur-trimmed coat wrapped around a curvy, frankly sexy body.

lines.japanese: 片言の日本語。甘ったるいフレグランス。馴れ馴れしい指先に光るネイルアート。はっきりしたエキゾチックな顔立ちは、美人だが俺の趣味ではなかった。
lines.english: Halting Japanese. Cloying perfume. Nail art glittering on fingers already pawing at me. Her sharply defined, exotic features were beautiful, though not to my taste.

lines.japanese: 女は断りもなく俺の横に居座り、ひとりで勝手に喋りつづける。一時間二万円のマッサージなんてどこの整体院よりも高いはずなのに、そいつはしきりに安いって言う。清く正しい俺には意味が分からない。
lines.english: She installed herself beside me without asking and proceeded to carry the conversation alone. Twenty thousand yen for an hour's massage had to be more than any legitimate clinic charged, yet she kept insisting it was cheap. Pure and upright citizen that I was, I had no idea what she meant.

lines.japanese: 俺は拙い日本語の誘い文句をかわしながら、逆に質問を投げかけたりして暇を潰してみた。しかし女があまりにセツい身の上話をあっけらかんと語りだすので、じきに居たたまれなくなってきた。
lines.english: I parried her halting sales pitch and passed the time by asking questions of my own. Then she began telling me an unbearably sad life story with such breezy matter-of-factness that I could no longer stand there.

lines.japanese: 弟たちによろしく。俺はそう言いのこし、片手を上げて女と別れた。プーの耳にはいろいろ辛い。休憩場所を変えよう。
lines.english: Give my regards to your brothers. With that, I raised a hand and left. Certain stories hit an unemployed man where it hurt. Time to take my break somewhere else.

lines.japanese: しかし、向かったアミューズメントビル下の簡易ベンチは満席だった。カラオケ待ちか、ダーツ帰りか、あるいはボウリング疲れの若い男女が囲むように占拠している。制服姿も交じってるチャラそうなガキ共──
lines.english: But every bench beneath the entertainment complex was taken. Young men and women ringed them—waiting for karaoke, coming back from darts, or exhausted from bowling. A flighty-looking crowd with a few school uniforms mixed in—

lines.japanese: ──いや、ちょっと待て、あれはもしや。
lines.english: —No. Wait. Could that be...?
“Ugh.”

lines.japanese: 羽虫の群れに、知ってる顔がいくつかあった。もちろん、どれも知りたくて知ったわけじゃない。
lines.english: Several familiar faces lurked among the moths. Naturally, I had learned none of them by choice.

lines.japanese: 一年前、俺は鳳翔にあの地下集会へ連れていかれて以来、やたら不良みたいなガキやおっさんに馴れ馴れしく声をかけられる機会が増えてしまったんだ。迷惑な話。
lines.english: In the year since Kakeru Otori took me to that underground gathering, delinquent-looking kids and grown men had developed an unfortunate habit of greeting me like an old friend. A considerable nuisance.

lines.japanese: 何が迷惑って、やつらは皇帝陛下の影響なのか、ちょっと気を許せばすぐにツケ上がる。知人→友人→親友へのランクアップがやけに早くて一方的、あーっという間に言動が図々しくなる。
lines.english: The problem was how quickly they started taking liberties the moment I relaxed, perhaps under the influence of His Imperial Majesty. They promoted themselves from acquaintance to friend to best friend at astonishing speed, entirely on their own, and turned shameless almost overnight.

lines.japanese: 「よーよー、そこの糞ニートぉ～！」
lines.english: “Yo, yo! Shitty unemployed bum!”

lines.japanese: だから俺は必要以上に無愛想オーラを出して、やつらの無礼講オーラを中和する必要があった。うざったく付きまとう街頭キャッチに、わざわざ笑顔を返してやったら逆効果だろ。そういう理屈。
lines.english: So I had to radiate extra hostility to cancel out their anything-goes chumminess. Smiling at a street tout who wouldn’t leave you alone only encouraged him. Same principle.

lines.japanese: 「うわシカト！？　ちょ待って！　待ってって、ねえ！　も、冗談だって隼人先ぱ～い！」
lines.english: “Whoa, you're ignoring me!? Wait! Wait up, come on! I was kidding, Hayato! Heeey, Hayato!”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　ハヤトぉ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Hayato?”

lines.japanese: 「うぞっ！　え、どこ！」
lines.english: “No way! Where?”

lines.japanese: 「らー、あっこ歩いてんじゃん。せんぷぁーい！　ハヤッせんぷぁーい！」
lines.english: “Look, he's right over there. Hayato! Hey, Hayato!”

lines.japanese: くそ、無視してたら騒ぎがよけいにデカくなってしまった。
lines.english: Dammit. Ignoring them had only made them louder.

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、声しぼれ声……」
lines.english: “Shut up. Turn the volume down...”

lines.japanese: つうか、名前を呼ぶな恥ずかしい。
lines.english: And quit shouting my name. It was embarrassing.

lines.japanese: めんどくせえから逃げるか、とも思ったが、しかし考えてみれば、この俺様が進もうと思ってた方向をわざわざこいつらのために変えるってのもおかしな話だ。
lines.english: I considered fleeing out of sheer annoyance. But when I thought about it, why should *I* change the direction I intended to walk for the sake of these people?

lines.japanese: 俺は舌打ちした口の形そのままに、ちょいと眉間をしぼってずんずん歩いた。ジャケットの脇ポケットで温めていた手は、あえてジーパンの前ポケットへ入れかえた。隼人はかっこよさが４上がった。
lines.english: I left my mouth twisted around the click of my tongue, drew my brows together, and marched on. I even transferred my hands from the warm side pockets of my jacket to the front pockets of my jeans. Hayato gained four points of coolness.

lines.japanese: 「アうーっそ！　マジ隼人君じゃーん！」
lines.english: “No waaay! It really is Hayato!”

lines.japanese: さっそく小娘が一匹、俺のアウトローな魅力にやられてベンチから走りよってきた。
lines.english: One little pest promptly succumbed to my outlaw magnetism and came running from the bench.

lines.japanese: 「えーなになになに、どしたんヘンな顔してー。虫歯ー？」
lines.english: “What, what, what? What's with the weird face? Toothache?”

lines.japanese: 俺は若干ショックを受けた。
lines.english: I sustained a modest shock.
“...Maybe.”

lines.japanese: そして仕方なく下顎をさすった。メンチきりながら。
lines.english: I had no choice but to rub my jaw, still glaring.

lines.japanese: 「えーカワイソちょお痛そーかもー、だいじょぶかー？」
lines.english: “Aww, poor thing. It looks like it hurts *so* bad. Are you okay?”

lines.japanese: もういい。ほっとけ。触んな、腕を触んな。
lines.english: Enough. Leave me alone. Don't touch me. Stop touching my arm.

lines.japanese: 「オー、マジで成田じゃん。かかか、久しぶりー！」
lines.english: “Oh, damn, it really is Narita! Ka-ka-ka! Been a while!”

lines.japanese: うるさい羽虫がもう一匹群れから離れて飛んできた。
lines.english: Another noisy moth detached itself from the swarm and flew over.

lines.japanese: 「ほい！　イェー、イェー、イェェェーイ！」
lines.english: “Here! Yeah! Yeah! Yeeeah!”

lines.japanese: やつは肘で直角に曲げた前腕を、右・左・両方とテンポ良く三回突きだしてきた。俺は同じ行動を求められていたはずだが、もちろん無視した。そういうのは気の知れたチャラ男同士でやっててくれ。
lines.english: He thrust his bent forearms toward me in three brisk beats—right, left, both. I was plainly expected to mirror him, and naturally ignored it. He could save that crap for party boys he was actually friends with.

lines.japanese: 「う～わ、完璧スルーされたよ。あーあー、ヒサビでミーツしてんのに、相変わらず冷たいよねーコイツ」
lines.english: “Whoa, completely blanked. Our first meet-up in forevs, and he’s still ice-cold.”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、もーホント南極類ヒト科だよねー、キンキンだもん凍る凍る。最近ぜんぜん絡んでくれんし、メール一個くんないとか、マジどんだけすかもぉー」
lines.english: “Right? He's seriously *Homo antarcticus*. Freezing—I'm freezing solid. He never gets involved with us anymore, never sends one message. Like, how much can one guy ignore you?”

lines.japanese: うるさい羽音。こいつら、きっと電車の中でも大声で喋るタイプだ。
lines.english: The irritating buzz continued. These two unquestionably talked at full volume on trains.

lines.japanese: げらげら笑ってる男の方──フルジップのジャケットをいちばん上まで閉めた、茶髪のロンゲが森里和馬。弱ええくせに皇帝・鳳の舎弟風吹かしていい気になってるやかましいやつ。
lines.english: The laughing boy—the long-haired guy with dyed-brown hair and his jacket zipped to the chin—was Kazuma Morisato. Weak as hell, yet pleased with himself for swaggering around like Emperor Otori’s lieutenant. Noisy.

lines.japanese: で、ツレの女──ポップめのカジュアルスタイルに口から白い棒を生やした女は香田亜衣。愛敬と馴れ馴れしさを履きちがえてるやかましいやつ。
lines.english: His female companion—the girl in bright casual clothes with a white stick sprouting from her mouth—was Ai Koda. She had mistaken invasive familiarity for charm. Also noisy.

lines.japanese: 鳳ンとこに女子部はないみたいだけど、このふたりが一緒につるんでるところはよく見る。まあ、大方ステディな関係なんだろう。どうでもいい。超どうでもいい。
lines.english: Otori’s outfit did not appear to have a women’s division, but I often saw these two together. Presumably they were going steady. I didn’t care. I really, really didn’t care.

lines.japanese: 「一ヵ月ぶりぐらいだっけぇー？　隼人君さー、もー、いいかげんケータイぐらい持っときー？」
lines.english: “Has it been about a month? Hayato, come on. At least get yourself a phone already.”

lines.japanese: 香田は棒付きキャンディを口から離し、その先端の玉っころを俺に向けて、くるくる円を描いた。
lines.english: Koda removed the lollipop from her mouth, aimed its little globe at me, and drew circles in the air.

lines.japanese: 「ほっとけ。巨大なお世話」
lines.english: “Leave me alone. That is monumentally none of your business.”

lines.japanese: 「あははっ、亜衣ぽん怒られたー。はははーん、うっせーばーか」
lines.english: “Ah ha ha! Poor little Ai got told off. Ha ha haaan. Shut up, stupid.”

lines.japanese: まったく堪えてない。香田は周囲が口汚いやつばかりで慣れてるのか、なかなかに逞しい小娘だった。
lines.english: She wasn’t fazed in the slightest. Perhaps everyone around Koda had such a filthy mouth that she had grown remarkably resilient.

lines.japanese: 「つか、逆にすげくね、いまどきケータイ持ってないとかそんな」
lines.english: “Actually, isn't it kind of incredible? Not owning a phone these days?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ、いいんだよ、俺は時代に流されない男なんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up, it's fine. I'm a man who refuses to drift with the times.”

lines.japanese: 「かっきー！　てか、要はオールウェイズ金欠だーん」
lines.english: “So coool! Meaning you're broooke all the time!”

lines.japanese: 「ちげーよ。いや、ちがくもねーけど……っせえな、いいんだよ。たとえ７兆円ぐらい持ってても、俺はケータイなんかいらねンだよ。べつに金の問題じゃねンだよ」
lines.english: “That's not it. I mean, it isn't *not* it... Shut up, it's fine. Even if I had seven trillion yen, I wouldn't want a phone. Money isn't the issue.”

lines.japanese: 「なー、もぉー！　そんな寂しーこと言ぅーなしー」
lines.english: “Come on! Don’t say something so lonely!”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ成田、それにいまの携帯電話って、通話とかメールだけじゃねーよ。カメラ、ネット、音楽、ゲームって、いろいろ用途あるしさ。コミュニケーションツールとして完結してねーから、持つだけ持っても……」
lines.english: “She's right, Narita. Phones these days aren't just for calls and messages. They've got cameras, internet, music, games—all kinds of uses. They aren't purely communication devices, so even without friends you could...”

lines.japanese: 「おー、ちょちょちょ待てコラ、なんだこの空気。なんで成田君ニハ友達イナイ前提で話が進んでんだ。しかもてめ、機械に弱いバアちゃん相手みてーな優しい声出してんじゃねえよ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Whoa, hold it. What’s with this atmosphere? Why are we moving ahead on the assumption that Narita Has No Friends? And quit using the gentle voice you’d use to explain technology to somebody’s grandmother. I’ll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「カズ君、なにげに携オタだもんね」
lines.english: “Kazu's kind of a secret phone geek.”

lines.japanese: 「オタゆーなよ。夏休みに若干ケータイショップでバイトしただけだって」
lines.english: “Don't call me a geek. I only worked at a phone shop for a little while over summer break.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そいぇばー、隼人君はいま何のバイトしてんの？」
lines.english: “Oh, speaking of that, Hayato, what job are you doing now?”

lines.japanese: 「つーかバイトしてんの？」
lines.english: “Wait, do you even have a job?”

lines.japanese: 遊興費目的でちょいちょいヌルいバイトしてる程度のお気楽学生が、いっぱしの社会人気取りでにやにやしていた。
lines.english: Carefree students who worked easy jobs now and then for spending money grinned at me like seasoned members of the workforce.

lines.japanese: 「あ～、ハイハイ、ひょっとしてアレまだ続けてるとか？　あの、なんか、クレープ屋の知り合いんトコお手伝いして回るやつ。人材派遣のままごと版みたいな」
lines.english: “Ahh, right. Are you still doing that thing? Running around helping people the crêpe lady knows. Like a kid's make-believe temp agency.”

lines.japanese: 「何でも屋は頼まれたときだけだっしょ？　普段は道路掘ったりビル壊したりだしょ？」
lines.english: “He only does handyman jobs when somebody asks, right? Normally he digs roads and demolishes buildings, doesn't he?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー」
lines.english: “Uh, well.”

lines.japanese: 話が好ましくない方へ転がりだした。だからベタベタするのは嫌なんだ。俺はまた無愛想オーラを強めて、ジーンズのポケットに手を突っ込んだ。隼人はおっかなさが４上がった。
lines.english: The conversation had begun rolling somewhere I didn't like. This was why I hated letting people get close. I intensified my hostile aura and shoved my hands into my jeans. Hayato gained four points of menace.

lines.japanese: 「つか俺、座りてーんだよ。オウ、どけほら」
lines.english: “More importantly, I want to sit. Move. Come on.”

lines.japanese: ふたりの間を割って進み、元やつらが座っていた無人のベンチにひとりでどっかり腰を落とした。
lines.english: I shouldered between them and dropped heavily onto the bench they had vacated.

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃはは最高！　隼人先輩、アンタ相変わらず感じわりーッスねえ！」
lines.english: “Gya-ha-ha, perfect! Hayato, you're still one unpleasant bastard!”

lines.japanese: 背もたれに後ろ向きでケツを預けていたギャル男が、肩越しに俺を振りかえって笑う。ベンチの周りでしゃがんでいた制服や私服の男女が、席ドロボーだの昼の電車にこーゆーババアいるよねなどと大声ではしゃいだ。
lines.english: The flashy kid, perched backward with his ass against the backrest, looked over one shoulder and laughed. The uniformed and casually dressed kids crouched around the bench erupted into cries of “Seat thief!” and “You see old ladies like that on daytime trains!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ナオジとかユキエとか初対面のやつ、とりま隼人先輩に挨拶しとけー？　このひとこんな、新機軸の大型芸人みたいなキャラしてっけど、ホンキ出しゃ翔さんの次ぐらいに強えーから。鬼だぜ鬼」
lines.english: “Hey, Naoji, Yukie—anybody meeting him for the first time, go say hello to Hayato. He may act like some revolutionary new breed of heavyweight comedian, but when he gets serious, he’s probably the strongest man after Kakeru. A demon. Seriously.”

lines.japanese: ギャル男はその集団のリーダー格だったみたいだ。適当なことを吹きこまれた手下だか後輩だかが、緊張気味のナンチャッテ敬語で次々に自己紹介しだした。俺は覚える気もなく、適当にオウヨと答えた。
lines.english: Apparently the flashy boy was the group’s leader. His followers or juniors, having swallowed that nonsense, began introducing themselves one by one in nervous make-believe politeness. With no intention of remembering any of them, I answered each with a careless “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「なあ大輔ぇー、あのホラ、成田にあの店教えてやればぁー？」
lines.english: “Hey, Daisuke, why don’t you tell Narita about that shop?”

lines.japanese: 言いながら森里が戻ってきた。やつの不愉快な股間が、俺の視界から柳木原の美しき夜景を塞いだ。
lines.english: Morisato returned as he spoke. His objectionable crotch eclipsed the beautiful Yanagihara nightscape.

lines.japanese: 「ホラおまえんとこの学校に、飛ばしのケータイ売ってる先輩いたじゃん。あの、なんか、止められるまでかけ放題のやつ？」
lines.english: “You know that older guy at your school who sells those untraceable phones? The ones you can call on all you want until the carrier cuts them off?”

lines.japanese: 「うわ。いらねえよ、んな、うさんくせー」
lines.english: “Ugh. Don’t want one. Shady as hell.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや！　それが全然、ノープロなの、ノープロブレム。べつに名前とか住所は必要ねーから、ぜってー足つかねーし。どうコレ、やばくね？　いや、やばいって、お得すぎでしょー」
lines.english: “No, no! Zero problemo. No problem. You don't need to give a name or address, so they can never trace it back to you. How insane is that? Seriously, it's too good a deal.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、おまえら使ってんのかよ」
lines.english: “Then do you use one?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか！　やだよ、んな、うさんくせー」
lines.english: “Hell no! Don’t want one. Shady as hell.”

lines.japanese: 「デスヨネーッ！」
lines.english: “Exactlyyy!”

lines.japanese: 「デスヨネじゃねえよ。あんさ？　テメーらさ、自販機のマズジュー試させる感覚でひとに不法な売買薦めるのとかやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Don't ‘exactly’ me. Listen. Could you quit recommending illegal transactions like you're daring somebody to try a disgusting new vending-machine drink?”

lines.japanese: 「つーか、もういいからロンゲ、おまえソコどけ。邪魔。見えねー」
lines.english: “And enough already, Longhair. Move. You’re in the way. I can’t see.”

lines.japanese: 「見えねー？　何が？」
lines.english: “Can’t see what?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせーな、おまえ以外のなんかだよ。おまえのクソうぜーロンゲ以外のなんかだよ。つか、おまえ髪切れ髪」
lines.english: “Shut up. Anything that isn’t you or your goddamn annoying hair. And get it cut.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: ブリーチされた茶色い眉をしかめて、森里がニヤケ面で見下ろしてくる。俺は負けずにベンチの上でふんぞりかえり、右の爪先を夜空の月へブッ刺してから、左の腿の上へ載せた。
lines.english: Morisato furrowed his bleached-brown brows and looked down at me through a smirk. Refusing to yield, I sprawled imperiously across the bench, stabbed the toe of my right shoe at the moon, then rested it on my left thigh.

lines.japanese: 「成田さあ……おまえそんな、いっつもタルそーな顔しちゃって、俺みたくニコニコできねえの？」
lines.english: “Narita... Do you always have to wear that exhausted face? Can't you smile like me?”

lines.japanese: 「おめーのはニヤニヤっつんだよ。あと、髪切れ髪」
lines.english: “Yours is called smirking. Also, cut your hair.”

lines.japanese: 「髪は関係ねーだろ髪はァ」
lines.english: “My hair has nothing to do with this!”

lines.japanese: 「あははっ」
lines.english: “Ah ha ha!”

lines.japanese: 耳障りな笑い声が弾けて、俺の横の隙間に、香水くさい体が尻から落ちてきた。
lines.english: An irritating laugh burst out, and a perfume-soaked body dropped ass-first into the space beside me.

lines.japanese: 「まーま、いいじゃんねー。隼人君オレ様キャラだし、愛想笑いとか似合わないもんねー」
lines.english: “Come on, it's fine. Hayato acts like he owns the world. A polite little smile wouldn't suit him.”

lines.japanese: 香田は俺の隣りに座って肩を擦りよせてくる。俺はケツをずらして距離を取った。やつの甘ったるい香水が胸にむかつきそうだったのと、森里が微妙な顔をしていたからだ。
lines.english: Koda sat beside me and rubbed her shoulder against mine. I shifted my ass away, partly because her syrupy perfume threatened to turn my stomach and partly because of the look on Morisato's face.

lines.japanese: 「やー、も端っこ痛すぎー」
lines.english: “Aww, sitting on the edge hurts.”

lines.japanese: しかし女はさらに詰めてきた。来んな。肩つけんな。
lines.english: But the girl only crowded closer. Stay back. Get your shoulder off me.

lines.japanese: 「ねーねー隼人君、最近どお？」
lines.english: “Hey, Hayato, how’ve things been lately?”

lines.japanese: 「ひみつ」
lines.english: “Secret.”

lines.japanese: 「いま何してたの？」
lines.english: “What were you doing just now?”

lines.japanese: 「ないしょ」
lines.english: “Classified.”

lines.japanese: 「このあと何すんの？」
lines.english: “What’re you doing after this?”

lines.japanese: 「おしえない」
lines.english: “Not telling.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー、そーなんだあー」
lines.english: “Ohh. Is that so?”

lines.japanese: ころころ。歯に飴玉の当たる脳天気な音が聞こえた。スティックの先端が左右に揺れる。
lines.english: *Clack, clack.* The carefree sound of candy knocking against teeth. The stick wagged from side to side.

lines.japanese: こんな無愛想な男相手にも笑顔を絶やさないんだから、考えようによっちゃこいつ、ものすごく心の広いやつなのかもしれない。
lines.english: Anyone who could keep smiling at a man this unfriendly had to be incredibly tolerant. Depending how you looked at it.

lines.japanese: ……ま、こいつら全員がそんな感じではあるけど。
lines.english: ...Though everyone in this crowd was much the same.

lines.japanese: 「そしたらさー、いまうちら、みんなでビリヤード行くとこなん、隼人君も一緒に行こっ？」
lines.english: “So, we’re all going to play pool now. Hayato, wanna come with us?”

lines.japanese: 「みんなでビリヤード」
lines.english: “All going to play pool.”

lines.japanese: 一瞬でも興味を引かれてしまった自分が嫌だった。
lines.english: I hated myself for finding the offer interesting, even for one second.

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいよ。んなヒマじゃねーし。おめーらも働け。な、汁流して働け」
lines.english: “No, thanks. I'm not that idle. You people should work too. Go on. Work up a sweat.”

lines.japanese: 「いいんだよ、俺らまだ学生だもん。つかゴメン、無職に説教垂れてほしくねーかも」
lines.english: “We're still students. Besides, sorry, but I don't think I want a lecture from an unemployed guy.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: ロンゲが俺を見下ろしてへらへら笑う。襟を立てて端まで閉めたジッパーのつまみが、顎の前でかすかに揺れていた。
lines.english: Longhair looked down and grinned at me. With his collar turned up and the zipper closed to its very end, the pull tab trembled faintly before his chin.

lines.japanese: 「んだてめ、無職なめんなコノヤロウ。無職はアレだぞホラ、磨かれてないダイヤ？　それだ、磨かれてねえんだよ。無限の可能性を秘めてんだよ。いいだろ、おまえ。毎日が自分探しだっつーの」
lines.english: “What the hell? Don't disrespect the unemployed, asshole. An unemployed man is—you know—a diamond in the rough. That's it. Unpolished. Brimming with limitless potential. Sounds nice, doesn't it? Every day is a journey of self-discovery.”

lines.japanese: 「そいや隼人先輩、この前やってたあの、道路工事のバイト？　アレまだ続けてる気味スか？」
lines.english: “Speaking of which, Hayato, that roadwork job you had before? You still kind of doing that?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、アレな……アレはまあ……アレだ、最近行ってない気味だけど」
lines.english: “Ahh, that... That one is... well. I sort of haven't been going lately.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なんでなんでー？」
lines.english: “What? Why, why?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでっておまえ……」
lines.english: “Why? Because...”

lines.japanese: こたえ、人間関係に疲れたから。言えるかバカヤロウ。
lines.english: Answer: human relationships had exhausted me. Like hell I could tell them that.

lines.japanese: 「っせーな、あんだよいろいろ。悪りぃかよ。あんだよ、いろいろ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Things happened. Got a problem with that? Things. Various things.”

lines.japanese: エージの言葉を借りるなら村八分。言わねっつのバカヤロウ。
lines.english: To borrow Eiji's melodramatic term, I had been cast out by the village. As if I was going to admit that, idiot.

lines.japanese: 「ほー、いろいろねぇ」
lines.english: “Oho. Stuff, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ニヤついてんじゃねーよタコ。てめ髪切れ、髪」
lines.english: “Quit smirking, jackass. Cut your hair.”

lines.japanese: 俺は紫色の空にパンと両手を合わせ、森里和馬が禿げますようにと祈った（八つ当たり）。
lines.english: I clapped both hands beneath the violet sky and prayed for Kazuma Morisato to go bald. Pure displaced aggression.

lines.japanese: 「そいじゃ隼人君、いまは何のバイトしてん？」
lines.english: “So, Hayato, what job are you doing now?”

lines.japanese: 「だから言ったじゃん。いまはアレだよあの、自分探し」
lines.english: “I told you. Right now I’m, you know, finding myself.”

lines.japanese: 「職探しか」
lines.english: “Finding a job.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、狭い意味で捉えりゃそういった側面もあるけどさ」
lines.english: “If you insist on the narrowest possible definition, yes, that is one aspect of it.”

lines.japanese: あ。言ってから後悔した。森里の前でする話じゃなかった。
lines.english: Ah. I regretted it the instant the words escaped. This was not a subject to raise before Morisato.

lines.japanese: 「は？　なんだ成田、バイト探してんの？　そんならウチで傭兵やりゃいーじゃん。成田ぐらい強けりゃ、翔さん、かなりカネ弾むんじゃね？」
lines.english: “What? Narita, you're looking for work? Then hire on with us as a mercenary. Somebody as strong as you—Kakeru would pay a hell of a lot.”

lines.japanese: ほら来た。くだらない。
lines.english: There it was. Ridiculous.

lines.japanese: 「はっ。傭兵だって。こえー」
lines.english: “Hah. A mercenary. Scary.”

lines.japanese: 俺は人差し指を対面の男に、首から上を横の女に向けた。
lines.english: I pointed one finger at the man across from me and turned my head toward the woman beside me.

lines.japanese: 「なに。こいつらいい歳して、まだそんな番長ごっこやってんの」
lines.english: “What, are these people still playing gang boss at their age?”

lines.japanese: 「だしょー、超だしょー？　も、マジありえんてぃー・てか、この子ら通称ドキュンだもん、隼人君からも言ってやってよー」
lines.english: “Right? Super right? It's completely impossiblissimo. These boys are textbook public nuisances, so you tell them, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 「かかか、仕方ねーじゃん。だって俺ら、ＴＶゲーム世代だもん。いくつンなっても虚構と現実の区別が付かねえんだってさ」
lines.english: “Ka-ka-ka. Can't be helped. We're the video-game generation. Apparently we'll never distinguish fiction from reality, however old we get.”

lines.japanese: 「あー！　まじだし、それ知ってるー。きょう朝のワイドショーで、だっちーの横の眼鏡が言ってた、アレでしょアレ、なんだっけ、成長ホルモンのバランスやらがー」
lines.english: “Oh! I know that one! The guy in glasses beside Datchi said it on a morning talk show today. Something about the balance of our growth hormones—”

lines.japanese: 「おお、見た見た俺も！　いーッや、今日のだっちーはまた、一段と嘘くさい胸してたねっ！」
lines.english: “Oh, I saw that too! Man, Datchi's chest looked even faker than usual today!”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょーちょー、なにそれ聞いてねえよ。あの巨乳パチモンなの」
lines.english: “What? Wait, nobody told me. Those enormous tits are counterfeit?”

lines.japanese: 「ネットじゃそーゆー話だよなー？　たしかに瞬発力テストんときの、あのガチィーン揺れなさは異常だったけどさあ」
lines.english: “That's what they say online, right? They didn't move one millimeter during the reflex test. Seriously unnatural.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょー！　うるせいよ貴様たち、いま胸の話なんかしてないじゃん！」
lines.english: “Hey! Shut up, you bastards. We weren't talking about her chest!”

lines.japanese: 「まじで？　え、なんの話だったっけ？」
lines.english: “Really? What were we talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、だっちーの横の眼鏡があ！」
lines.english: “The guy in glasses next to Datchi said—”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、眼鏡なに言ってたっけ？」
lines.english: “Wait. What did Glasses say?”

lines.japanese: 「つうかよー、朝のワイドショーなんて、普通だっちーの胸しか見ねえだろー」
lines.english: “Who watches a morning wide show for anything but Datchi's tits?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、普通はその番組自体観ねえだろ。おー、おまえら大学生でもないのに、なに優雅な朝過ごしてんだよ。ガッコ行けガッコ」
lines.english: “Normal people don't watch the program at all. Why are you enjoying such elegant mornings when you aren't even college students? Go to school.”

lines.japanese: 「うんー、行くときは行くケレドモさー。なーんかビミョーに浮いてる気なんだよねー、私」
lines.english: “Yeah, I go when I go. But I sort of feel faintly out of place there.”

lines.japanese: 「ビミョーならまだいいじゃん、俺なんかフツーに浮いてんだぜえ。そんで追い打ち、三年に上がったらセントヘレナに島流しとかゆっちゃってー。つか、ゆわれちゃってー」
lines.english: “Faintly is still good. I’m openly out of place. Then, for the finishing blow, when I move up to third year they’re exiling me to Saint Helena. Or rather, that’s what they told me.”

lines.japanese: 「ゆわるる隔離学級っしょー？　あんね、そーゆーノリってね、うちのパパの世代だと、なんか腐ったミカンの方程式たら言うんだってー。ミカンだよミカン？　段々畑かっつーのコレ超ウケない？」
lines.english: “The so-called isolation class, right? See, in my dad’s generation they apparently called that ‘the rotten-orange equation.’ An orange! What is this, a terraced orchard? Isn’t that hilarious?”

lines.japanese: 「マぁジだぁー。ぎゃはは、そーりゃおまえ、あんなゴリゴリの進学校、行く方が悪りぃだろ。つか、行かねーだろフツー。ええ和馬ァ、中途半端にアタマよろしいと苦労されますなァー」
lines.english: “Seriously? Gya-ha-ha! That's what you get for entering such an intense prep school. Normal people don't. Kazuma, how difficult life must be when you're moderately intelligent.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それホントそーだわ。あのガッコひでえもん、あんなん公開イジメだァ、テンションだだ下がりだわ。出来のワリー子の学習意欲、さらに削いでどーすんだっつーの！　アホか、死ね、退学上等！」
lines.english: “No, seriously. That school is awful. It's public humiliation. Kills your motivation dead. What do they gain by taking the bad students and crushing whatever desire to learn they have left? Idiots. Die. Expel me—I dare you!”

lines.japanese: よく分からないが、森里はなにやら体制の傲慢に憤慨しているご様子。ロックだ。
lines.english: I did not entirely follow, but Morisato appeared incensed by the arrogance of the system. Rock and roll.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そだ！　隼人先輩さあ、そんじゃビリヤードはいいんでー、あの、ちょっとばかし『ヘテロ』寄ってってくんないスかー」
lines.english: “Oh, right! Hayato, if pool's out, could you at least stop by Hetero for a little while?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ヘテ……なんだって？」
lines.english: “Huh? Hetero... what?”

lines.japanese: 「ヘテロっすよ、ヘテロクロミア。ほら、あんた前に行ってンしょ。あの、俺らと最初に会った地下の」
lines.english: “Hetero. Heterochromia. You've been there—the underground place where you first met us.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あの犯罪の温床。え、でもあそこ潰れたんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Oh, the incubator of crime. Wait, didn't it close?”

lines.japanese: 「だから。前の店が潰れて、そこに出来た新しい店のことだろ。おまえクラブなんて、しょっちゅう“潰れちゃ出来て潰れちゃ出来て”すんだから。そんなん考えなくても分かンだろ、ちったあ考えろよ」
lines.english: “That's the point. The old place closed and a new one opened on the same site. Clubs are forever closing and opening and closing and opening. You could figure that out without thinking. Use your head once in a while.”

lines.japanese: 考えても考えなくても怒られるのか。なんて理不尽な。俺はなぜか偉そうな森里をスルーして、隣りの保護者に訊いた。
lines.english: So I got scolded whether I thought or didn't think. How unreasonable. Ignoring the inexplicably superior Morisato, I consulted the guardian beside him.

lines.japanese: 「なあ香田。このうざいロンゲの男の子、なんでいつも俺に反抗的なの」
lines.english: “Hey, Koda. Why is this irritating long-haired boy always so rebellious toward me?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、嫉妬嫉妬。ほら、いとしの翔さんが隼人君にばっかギラついてっから、もうミッシューミッシューゆっちゃって全力ロンリーほとばしってんの」
lines.english: “Oh, jealousy, jealousy. His beloved Kakeru only has eyes for you, so Kazu's all *miss you, miss you*, spraying maximum-strength loneliness everywhere.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、あの、冗談でもそーゆーアブノマな設定とかやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa. Could you quit inventing creepy little fantasies like that, even as a joke?”

lines.japanese: 「ほんっと！　ヘッ、んなワケねーだろが」
lines.english: “Exactly! Hah. As if.”

lines.japanese: 禁断の愛だの、秘密の花園だのと、薔薇色の冷やかしがワーキャー飛ぶ中、森里は独り言のように吐きすてた。
lines.english: Forbidden love, secret gardens, rose-colored teasing—the delighted cries flew around him while Morisato spat the words as though speaking to himself.

lines.japanese: 「俺も成田もＹＦＢのみんなも、あのひとにとっちゃ全員ハナから眼中ねンだよ」
lines.english: “Me, Narita, everyone in the YFB—we were never in that man's sights from the start.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　和馬なんか言った？」
lines.english: “Huh? Kazuma, did you say something?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「あそう」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「でよー、ねー、頼んますよ隼人先ぱーい。とりまヘテロ行ってくださいってー。場所分かんねーなら、俺ら一緒に付いてきますからさー。なー行こうぜー」
lines.english: “So come on, please, Hayato. Just go to Hetero for now. If you don't know the way, we'll come with you. Come on, let's go.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いま丁度あっこに皇帝いるから。ね？　隼人先輩的にも会いたいっしょー、翔さん」
lines.english: “Because the Emperor happens to be there right now. You want to see Kakeru too, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 俺は嫌悪感もあらわに顔をしかめた。
lines.english: My face twisted in undisguised revulsion.

lines.japanese: 「やだよ。尚更やだよ。あいつ超イミフだし、日本語通じねンだもん」
lines.english: “No. Even less now. That man makes absolutely no sense, and Japanese doesn't work on him.”

lines.japanese: 「んーな、ちょっせーこと言うなよお。ちょっと顔貸すぐらい、べつにいいじゃーん。だって俺、隼人先輩見っけといてヘテロ連れてけなかったら、皇帝にメンツ立たねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Come on, don't be so stingy. You can show your face for a minute. If I find Hayato and fail to bring him back to Hetero, I lose face with the Emperor.”

lines.japanese: 「知るかよ、非行少年のメンツなんか」
lines.english: “Why should I care about a juvenile delinquent’s face?”

lines.japanese: 「なーりた、オメ非行少年ゆーなってェ。俺ら、毒もって毒制してるだけじゃんよ。柳木原フレイムバーズは正義の味方なんだぜえ。なあ？」
lines.english: “Narita, don't call us juvenile delinquents. Sometimes it takes poison to beat poison. The Yanagihara Flame Birds are champions of justice. Right?”

lines.japanese: 森里が白々しく手を広げると、小僧たちは肩を揺らしてそーだそーだと適当に笑った。どいつもこいつも白々しい。
lines.english: Morisato spread his hands with patent insincerity. The kids shook their shoulders and laughed a careless chorus of agreement. Every last one of them was full of it.

lines.japanese: 「正義の味方ァ？」
lines.english: “Champions of justice?”

lines.japanese: ハハ。こっちこそ肩を揺らした。なーにが正義の味方だ。先生方もお巡りさんも地域住民の皆さんも、本当はこいつら自身でさえも、誰ひとりそんな風には思っちゃいない。
lines.english: Ha. Now my shoulders were shaking. Champions of justice, my ass. Their teachers didn't think so, the police didn't think so, the neighborhood residents didn't think so. The truth was, not one of these kids thought so either.

lines.japanese: 凶暴性をちらつかせて街に群がる。弱いものを睨む。強いものを叩く。エアロパーツごてごてのワンボックスを停めて、バックドアからフルボリュームのギャングスタ・ラップを垂れながす。
lines.english: They swarmed the city with their capacity for violence on display. Glared at the weak. Struck the strong. Parked vans buried under body kits and blasted gangsta rap at full volume through the open rear doors.

lines.japanese: やつらはそれが、他のやんちゃなガキ共をビビらせる「犯罪を未然に防ぐための示威行動」だなんてもっともらしいことを言うけれど、健全な一般市民からすればただの集団非行、もっと言えば迷惑防止条例違反だ。
lines.english: They solemnly called this ‘a show of force intended to prevent crime’ by intimidating other unruly kids. To ordinary law-abiding citizens, it was gang delinquency—more precisely, a violation of the public-nuisance ordinance.

lines.japanese: さて──
lines.english: Now, then—

lines.japanese: ──悪いがここでひとつ、俺が以前こいつらに聞かされた、とてもつまんない昔話をしよう。
lines.english: —and here, regrettably, I must tell you a profoundly boring old tale they once told me.

lines.japanese: むかしむかしあるところに、草フットサルの青年チームがひとつありました。名前は忘れた。それはあんまし重要じゃないんだ。仮にカメさんチームとでもしとこう。
lines.english: Once upon a time, there was an amateur youth futsal team. I forget the name. It isn't important. Let us call them Team Tortoise.

lines.japanese: ある頃からカメさんチームは、ゲーム中のクロスプレイが元で、ガラの悪いウサギさんチームにイジワルをされるようになりました。主にコート外で。ウサギさんチームにはおっかないお友達がたくさんいたのです。
lines.english: One day, after a collision during a game, a rough crowd called Team Hare began bullying Team Tortoise—mostly off the court. Team Hare had a great many frightening friends.

lines.japanese: カメさんチームが困っていると、たまたま腕っぷしの強いニワトリさんに出くわしました。事情を打ちあけ思いきって助力を求めてみると、ニワトリさんもちょうど暇と体力を持てあましていたので応じてくれました。
lines.english: In their distress, the tortoises happened upon a chicken of extraordinary physical strength. They told him their troubles and bravely asked for help. The chicken had time and energy to spare, so he agreed.

lines.japanese: ちなみに本末転倒な話ですが、この頃にはもうカメさんたちはフットサルを忘れて、とにかくナメられないようにと外国の不良みたいな格好をするようになっておりました。
lines.english: The whole affair had the cart before the horse: by this point the tortoises had forgotten futsal entirely. Their sole concern was not being looked down on, and they had begun dressing like foreign hoodlums.

lines.japanese: さて、士気上がるカメさんたち、用心棒を連れていざ決戦場へ。時代劇で言うところの「先生やっちゃってください」ってやつです。さあ、ニワトリ先生の大暴れ、たちまちウサギさんチームはコテンパンです。
lines.english: Thus heartened, the tortoises marched with their bodyguard to the field of battle. In an old samurai movie, this was the moment for “Get ’em, boss.” Then the chicken went wild, and Team Hare lay flattened in no time.

lines.japanese: ぴょんぴょん跳ねて喜ぶカメさんたちと、丸くなって地に伏すウサギさんたち。彼ら全員にニワトリ先生が言いました。「両軍とも良くがんばりました。これからはお互い力を合わせ、さらなる敵に挑むのです」。
lines.english: The tortoises hopped with delight; the hares curled into balls upon the ground. The chicken addressed them all. ‘Both armies fought admirably. From this day forward, combine your strength and challenge still greater enemies.’

lines.japanese: さて、ウサギ団とカメ団が同盟を結んだという噂はたちまち都じゅうに広まりました。新参者にデカい顔をさせちゃなるまいと、今度はオオカミさんチームやライオンさんチームが次々に戦争をしかけてきます。
lines.english: News of the alliance between Hare and Tortoise soon spread throughout the capital. Team Wolf and Team Lion, unwilling to let the newcomers swagger around unchecked, declared war one after another.

lines.japanese: 彼らはニワトリ先生を旗印に迫りくる悪いやつらをちぎっては投げちぎっては投げ、そうして傘下あるいは同盟国を増やしてゆき、いつしか柳木原の悪を蹴散らす“私設自警団”なんて名乗るようになりましたとさ。
lines.english: With the chicken as their banner, they hurled aside every villain who came against them. Their affiliates and allies multiplied until one day they styled themselves a “private neighborhood watch” that swept evil from Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: めでたくなし、めでたくなし。
lines.english: And they did not live happily ever after.

lines.japanese: 「ちゅーわけで隼人先輩、ヘテロ行こーよ。ね、行っちゃえばいいジャン、朝まで踊っちゃえばいいジャン」
lines.english: “So that's the story, Hayato. Come to Hetero. Come on, you can just go, right? You can just dance till morning, right?”

lines.japanese: 「いいジャンつうか、そんじゃリアルな話すっけど、ぶっちゃけ俺いまクラブ行く金なんかねーし」
lines.english: “Never mind what I can ‘just’ do. Here’s the real-world problem: I honestly don’t have money for a club right now.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　なんでよ、金ってそんなん、隼人先輩なら顔パスだし関係ねーって。しかも実は今日ね……あ、コレ内緒内緒、コレここだけの話だから。いい？　あんね、こっから先はぜってー部外者に漏らすの禁止ね」
lines.english: “What? Money doesn’t matter. You’re Hayato—they’ll wave you straight in. And actually, tonight... Oh, secret, secret. This stays right here, okay? Nothing beyond this point can leak to outsiders.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、その、あたかも俺が部外者じゃないみたいな前置きやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa. Could you quit saying that like I’m not an outsider?”

lines.japanese: 「いや実はね、ヘテロがクローズしたあと、俺ら会場移してアフターやんスよ」
lines.english: “See, after Hetero closes, we're changing venues for an after-party.”

lines.japanese: 「アフターって、二次会か」
lines.english: “After-party? A second round?”

lines.japanese: 「題してトワイライト・レイヴ・パーティー！　夜明けの狂乱祭り！　ってゆうね、趣旨のね」
lines.english: “We call it the Twilight Rave Party! A riotous festival at dawn! That’s the concept.”

lines.japanese: 「へー。どっかの駐車場でゲリラレイヴでもやんの」
lines.english: “Huh. Throwing a guerrilla rave in some parking lot?”

lines.japanese: 「ヒント。正義と平和を愛する私設自警団・柳木原フレイムバーズは、この街の風紀を乱す非行集団と日夜戦いつづけているのであった！」
lines.english: “Hint. The Yanagihara Flame Birds, a private neighborhood watch devoted to justice and peace, wage ceaseless battle against delinquent groups that corrupt the morals of our city!”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、もしかして……」
lines.english: “Ugh. You can’t mean...”

lines.japanese: 「そ。ぶっちゃけ言うと、ブッコミっすよブッコミ」
lines.english: “Right. Bluntly, we're storming their turf.”

lines.japanese: 「うーわ、気が滅入った。なんだこいつら。俺ブッコミって言葉、ヤンキー漫画以外で初めて聞いたわ」
lines.english: “God, that’s depressing. What is wrong with you people? I’ve never heard anybody talk about ‘storming enemy turf’ outside a delinquent manga.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いま大輔ン中で昭和ブーム来てっから」
lines.english: “Oh, Daisuke’s on an eighties kick right now.”

lines.japanese: 「ゲロゲロ～？　ブッ飛び～！　みたいなァ！？」
lines.english: “Grodyyy! Totally rad! Like that!?”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃはは聖戦だぜ聖戦。も、ボッコボコにしちゃうけどね、ボクら正義の味方ですから！　とかゆってぇ！　くはー、俄然アガるわー！　コレもう、隼人先輩も来るっしょ、来るしかないっしょハー！」
lines.english: “Gya-ha-ha, it’s a holy war. Holy war. We’ll beat them into paste, but hey, we’re champions of justice! Or something! Ahh, I’m suddenly pumped! You’ve got to come now, Hayato. You don’t have a choice!”

lines.japanese: 「行かねーよ。だから俺、これから仕事あんだって」
lines.english: “I’m not going. I told you, I have work after this.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、なくても絶対行かねーけど」
lines.english: “Even if I didn’t, I’d never go.”

lines.japanese: <20>\「えええエェーッ！！？」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: 「エーじゃねえよ。いまの発言に度肝抜く要素なんかどこにもねえよ。完璧キャラ通りの反応だよ」
lines.english: “Don't ‘what’ me. There was nothing remotely shocking about that statement. It was a perfectly in-character response.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　でもさー成田工務店、おまえ何でも屋なんだろー？　ほんじゃさ、仕事としてウチの手伝い請けおえよ。金なら翔さんが出すだろうし。そんなら異論はねーだろ？」
lines.english: “Wait, Narita Construction. You're a handyman, right? Then take a paid job helping us. Kakeru will put up the money. You can't object to that.”

lines.japanese: 「あるよ。やだよ。金の問題じゃねーっつうの」
lines.english: “I can. I don't want to. Money isn't the issue.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そ？　ふーん、もったいない。翔さんなら、すんーげえ報酬出すんだろうに」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah? Huh. What a waste. Kakeru would probably pay serious money.”

lines.japanese: 「え……たとえばどんぐらい」
lines.english: “Like... how much, for example?”

lines.japanese: 俺の心はちょっぴり揺らいだ。
lines.english: My resolve wavered by a hair.

lines.japanese: 「いや、具体的な額はバメンだけどー。ほんでも皇帝、めためたカネモだもん。オイオイやばいぜぇ、シャキィーン立っちゃうかもよォ、給料袋～」
lines.english: “Couldn't name a figure without knowing the job. But the Emperor is seriously loaded. Oh, man, it might stand straight up—your pay envelope, I mean!”

lines.japanese: 「あれっ？　気ぃ変わった？」
lines.english: “Oh? Change your mind?”

lines.japanese: 「か、変わってねえよ。変わるわけねえだろ。ほんとだよ。ああッ、んだテメ、ニヤニヤしてんじゃねえブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。おし」
lines.english: “N-no. Of course not. No chance. I mean it. Hey, what the hell are you smirking at? I'll fucking kill you, asshole. I'll fucking kill you, asshole. All right.”

lines.japanese: 自分を取りもどした俺は、改めて気を引きしめた。
lines.english: I came back to my senses and steeled myself again.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ隼人先輩、Ｒ－ウィングってチーム知ってる？　知らねえか！　んーと、まあ、規模はそんなデカい方じゃねーんだけど、なんてーか、キモくて目障りでヤバい連中でさあコレ！」
lines.english: “So, Hayato, know a team called R-Wing? Probably not. They aren't one of the bigger outfits, but they're creepy, irritating, and dangerous as hell!”

lines.japanese: いや、おまえらの皇帝よりキモくて目障りでヤバいやつなんて、この街のどこ探したっていねーだろ。
lines.english: As if there were anybody in this whole town creepier, more irritating, or more dangerous than their Emperor.

lines.japanese: 「でぇ、ここんとこウチら、そいつらとボチボチ戦りあってんだけどー」
lines.english: “So lately we’ve been fighting them here and there.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。なんで」
lines.english: “Huh. Why?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、なんでとかじゃなくて。聖戦だから聖戦。害虫駆除。正義のおしごと」
lines.english: “Come on, it isn't about why. It's a holy war. Pest control. The work of justice.”

lines.japanese: 答えになってねえ。と思ったけど、面倒なので黙っておいた。
lines.english: That wasn’t an answer, but arguing sounded like too much trouble, so I kept quiet.

lines.japanese: 「まー、そいつらがなんか、イッちゃってるっつーか？　そう、リアルでイッちゃってる感じなの。ありゃシャレ抜きでサイコ入ってんだろ、別の意味でこええよ」
lines.english: “They're kind of far gone, you know? For real. There's something genuinely psychotic about them. Scary in a completely different way.”

lines.japanese: 「言えてる。どーもウチとはノリが違うんだよねえ」
lines.english: “True. They don’t operate on the same wavelength as us.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　そんなん言ったら、おまえらだってギャル男とかＢ系とかレゲエ風とか、全然バラバラで統一感ねーじゃん。つか鳳なんか、あいつこそまさしくサイコ入ってるし」
lines.english: “Huh? By that standard, you've got a fashion-plate pretty boy, a B-boy, and a reggae wannabe. None of you match. And Otori is the clearest psycho of all.”

lines.japanese: 「ちっげえよ、そーゆーシュミとかカッコの話じゃなくてえ！　じゃなくて、もっとこう根本的なさあ、あの、あんじゃん。だから目的意識っつうか、その……行動原理？」
lines.english: “That's not what I mean! I'm not talking about tastes or clothes. It's something more fundamental. You know—their purpose, or... what drives them?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: うさんくさい単語が出てきた。半人前ヤンキーの自分語りほどウザったいものはない。俺は目を腫れぼったく見開きながらキョトキョトよそ見して、わたしは君たちの話に関心を示していませんよオーラで対抗した。
lines.english: Out came the dubious jargon. Nothing was more tiresome than a half-baked delinquent explaining his philosophy of life. I opened my puffy eyes wide and looked pointedly everywhere else, fighting back with an aura that declared: *I have no interest whatsoever in this conversation.*

lines.japanese: 「あー、なんて言やいいんだ……和馬、ちょっと俺らの言いたいこと隼人先輩に説明しろよ。おまえ、頭だけは俺よりマシなんだし」
lines.english: “Ahh, how do I put it... Kazuma, explain what we’re trying to say to Hayato. At least you’ve got more brains than me.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ、頭は関係ねーけど……アレだろ要するに、あの、なんで俺らツルんでるのかっちゅー。集合行為の潜在心理みたいな」
lines.english: “Hah. It isn't about brains, but... basically, why we all come together. The hidden psychology of collective behavior, or something.”

lines.japanese: 「ソレだ！　分かんねーけど、たぶんソレだ。おー、言ってやって言ってやって」
lines.english: “That! I don't understand it, but that's probably it. Go on, tell him.”

lines.japanese: 「いやまァ、だから極端なこと言っちゃえばだよ。俺らはただ、遊んでる、だけなんだよ。いや、遊ぶってアレね、あの女は遊んでそーとか、そっちの遊ぶじゃなくて。幼稚園児でも知ってる方の、無邪気な遊ぶね」
lines.english: “Well, to put it in the most extreme terms, we're only playing. And I don't mean *playing around* as in ‘that woman looks like she plays around.’ I mean innocent play, the kind every kindergartner understands.”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、ガキのころさ、みんな校庭とか広場に集まって、鬼ごっこだドッジボールだって遊んでたじゃん。その流れなのよ。そのラインなの。その延長線上に立ってるだけなの、いまの俺らって」
lines.english: “Remember being kids? Everybody met in the schoolyard or the park and played tag or dodgeball. This is just the same thing carried forward. That's all we are now: an extension of what we were then.”

lines.japanese: 「おお！　なんかイイじゃん、いいこと言ってる気じゃん」
lines.english: “Whoa! That sounds good. Feels like you're saying something profound.”

lines.japanese: 「でもそれがさ、いつの間にか歳取って、いつの間にか体もでかくなっちゃって、そんで、いつの間にか鬼ごっことかドッジボールしなくなってて、つか、そもそも今じゃ、遊ぶなんて単語自体がなんか照れッけど──」
lines.english: “But somewhere along the way we got older, somewhere along the way our bodies got bigger, and somewhere along the way we stopped playing tag and dodgeball. Hell, now even saying the word *play* is a little embarrassing—”

lines.japanese: 「──でも、そーゆーことでしょ？　感覚的には大して変わってなくね？　俺ら遊んでんだよ。あの頃のままなの、同じ同じ。気付いてないやつも多いけど、結局みんな心に形のないドッジボール持ってんの」
lines.english: “—but isn't that what this is? The feeling hasn't really changed. We're playing. We're still the same kids. Lots of people never notice it, but everybody carries a shapeless dodgeball in their heart.”

lines.japanese: 「形のないドッジボール！　いいねソレ、いま俺チョー赤線引きてえ。つかコレ出るぜ、期末出るぜマジで」
lines.english: “A shapeless dodgeball! That's good. I want to underline that in red right now. Seriously, that's going to be on the final. Guaranteed.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ、だからみんな遊びたいの。疼いてんだよ、その、ボール持ってる心が。ボールってか、まあ、ひとによっちゃゲームだったりお人形だったりすんだろうけど、うん、それは各人の思い出次第よ」
lines.english: “Right. Everybody wants to play. That heart with the ball inside it starts to ache. For some people it might be a video game or a doll instead. That depends on what they remember.”

lines.japanese: 「おーし、そんじゃまー遊ぼっかー、つって。とりあえず暇なやつ遊ぼーぜー、つって。そんでなんとなーく集まってみたら、なんとなーくナウこんな感じになってるわけだけど」
lines.english: “So we say, all right, let's play. Anybody free, come play. We drift together, and somehow this is what we've ended up with.”

lines.japanese: 「イェス！　いや、いいわ和馬。おまえ、俺の言いてーこと８２パー代弁してくれた。マジ、見直した。すげーおまえ、俺ァもう驚きのあまり我が耳を職務質問だね！」
lines.english: “Yes! Damn, Kazuma, that was good. You said eighty-two percent of what I wanted to say. Seriously, I have newfound respect for you. I'm so amazed I'm taking my own ears downtown for questioning!”

lines.japanese: 「マだから話戻ッけど、そのＲ－ウィングっつー連中は、そこンとこがウチと違げーのよ。なんかマジ過ぎるッつーか？　宗教がかってるつーか？　アホだぜアホ。もー、遊びゴコロ足りなくてよー」
lines.english: “But back to the point: that's where R-Wing differs from us. They're too serious, you know? Almost religious? Idiots. They don't know how to play.”

lines.japanese: 「そーそ、必死過ぎてシラけんだよね。学校でもいんじゃん、ホラ、授業のサッカーとか本息でゴリゴリいっちゃって、周りにおもくそ引かれてるタイプ。あァ、でも成田なんておまえ、案外そういう──」
lines.english: “Right, right. They try so hard it kills the mood. You know the type at school—the guy who goes full contact in gym-class soccer while everybody else backs away? Though Narita, come to think of it, you might be exactly—”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ香田おまえ、アレは知ってるアレ。ジンクピリチオン」
lines.english: “Hey, Koda, know what zinc pyrithione is?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なにソレ初知りー」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that? Never heard of it.”

lines.japanese: 「──ってオイィィィ！　おま、話聞けよ！　私語慎めよ！」
lines.english: “—Heyyy! Listen when I'm talking! No side conversations!”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　馬鹿かおまえ、聞いてほしかったらもっと面白トーク展開しろよ。ジンクピリチオンの話とかしてみろよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Idiot, if you want me to listen, say something interesting. Try talking about zinc pyrithione.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。カズ君たちの話つまんない。てゆかイタい」
lines.english: “Yeah. You guys are boring. Actually, you're painful to watch.”

lines.japanese: 「なっ、なんだよコーダイン！　おめ、どっちの味方だよ！」
lines.english: “What the hell, Kodine? Whose side are you on?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでー。隼人君の方に決まってんじゃん、ねーっ」
lines.english: “Why? Hayato's side, obviously. Right?”

lines.japanese: 香田が体ごと俺の腕にしがみついてきた。鼻をつく香水。なだらかで硬い胸の感触。森里のにやけた仮面に分かりやすくヒビが入った。
lines.english: Koda wrapped her entire body around my arm. Perfume stabbed my nose. The smooth, firm pressure of her chest. A visible crack ran through Morisato's smirking mask.

lines.japanese: 「いらねーよ、触んな」
lines.english: “Don’t want it. Get off.”

lines.japanese: 俺はきっぱり拒絶して、やつの腕を振りほどいた。嫉妬深い男にくだらない誤解をされたらたまったもんじゃない。
lines.english: I refused her flatly and shook her off. The last thing I needed was some jealous man getting the wrong idea.

lines.japanese: 「うゎ、ひっどぉー！　も、何そのリアクション。信じらんない！　えぐられた！」
lines.english: “Whoa, horrible! What kind of reaction is that? I can't believe you! You cut me deep!”

lines.japanese: 耳の穴にダイレクトで飛びこんでくるキンキン声。うざい。男だったらひっぱたいてる。
lines.english: Her shrill voice flew directly into my ear canal. Annoying. Had she been a man, I would have slapped her.

lines.japanese: 「心の痛み！　心の痛み！」
lines.english: “Pain in my heart! Pain in my heart!”

lines.japanese: 香田はわけ分かんないことを言いながら、腕を振りまわして俺の体にぶつけはじめた。そのそよ風みたいな暴力に吹かれながら、俺は森里に言った。
lines.english: Spouting incomprehensible protests, Koda swung her arms and began thumping me. Buffeted by that breeze-like violence, I addressed Morisato.

lines.japanese: 「おいハゲ。このクソうぜー女、なんとかしろ」
lines.english: “Hey, Baldy. Do something about this obnoxious woman.”

lines.japanese: 「ハゲてねーよ、ハゲ」
lines.english: “I’m not bald, Baldy.”

lines.japanese: やつは目蓋を半分閉じて鼻筋にしわを刻みながら、その長い髪に正面から指を通して、がーっと後ろまで流した。
lines.english: Eyes half-lidded and nose wrinkled, he drove his fingers through his long hair from the front and swept it violently backward.

lines.japanese: 「亜衣。うぜー言われてっから」
lines.english: “Ai. He says you’re annoying.”

lines.japanese: 「うざくなーいー！」
lines.english: “I am noooot!”

lines.japanese: 森里に肩を叩かれると、香田は反抗期の子供みたいに暴れてそれを払いのけ、またぞろ俺の腕にしがみついてきた。なだらかな硬い感触。俺は腕を引きぬいた。
lines.english: When Morisato touched her shoulder, Koda thrashed like a rebellious child and slapped his hand away, then latched onto my arm again. That smooth firmness. I pulled free.

lines.japanese: 「だーら、触んなっつんだよもう。女くせえの移んだろ。あとソレ、おまえパット厚過ぎ」
lines.english: “I keep telling you, stop touching me. You'll get girl stink all over me. Also, those pads are way too thick.”

lines.japanese: 「うぞっ！？」
lines.english: “No way!?”

lines.japanese: 女は慌てて体を引いて、両手で自分の胸をふたつ鷲掴みした。なんかエロいポーズ。
lines.english: The girl sprang away and seized both breasts in her hands. A strangely erotic pose.

lines.japanese: 「え……バレバレ？」
lines.english: “Wait... completely obvious?”

lines.japanese: 「まー、バレぐらいだな」
lines.english: “Obvious enough.”

lines.japanese: 香田の耳が赤くなった。珍しい。その辺は意外に純情だったみたいだ。
lines.english: Koda's ears reddened. Unusual. Apparently she was surprisingly innocent in that department.

lines.japanese: 「……へぇーえ。おまえ、そんなんしてたんだぁ」
lines.english: “...Ohhh. So you've been doing that.”

lines.japanese: 森里の反応は笑ってるんだか拗ねてるんだかよく分からない。いや、なんだか照れて気まずそうだ。
lines.english: I couldn't tell whether Morisato was laughing or sulking. No—he looked embarrassed and awkward.

lines.japanese: ん？　あれ、なんだこいつ、彼氏のくせに知らなかったのか。
lines.english: Hm? Wait. He was her boyfriend and did not know?

lines.japanese: ふうん。こいつら、どうせ発情期の犬猫みたいな節操ない付き合いしてんのかと思ったら、意外とプラトニックなんだな。まー、いーんじゃねえの。俺の中でちょっとだけ好感度が上がった。
lines.english: Huh. I had assumed they conducted their relationship with all the restraint of animals in heat, but apparently they were surprisingly chaste. Well, good for them. They rose slightly in my estimation.

lines.japanese: 「うぅー、もう超っパズだー……わざわざみんなの前でばらすとか、どんだけＳだよもー、ばかやろー」
lines.english: “Ugh, this is so mortifying... You had to expose me in front of everybody? How much of a sadist are you? God, you jerk.”

lines.japanese: 「あー悪り悪り、ほんと悪り」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry, sorry. Seriously.”

lines.japanese: 「……え、ちょっと待って。いまの俺が悪いの。いや、悪いか。ん、どうなん？」
lines.english: “...Wait. Was that my fault? I mean, I guess it was. Hm. What's the ruling?”

lines.japanese: 森里に判断を仰いだつもりが、やつはいつの間にやら携帯電話をカチカチいじっていて、俺の言葉など聞いちゃいなかった。
lines.english: I meant to ask Morisato for a ruling, but at some point he had started clicking away at his phone and had heard none of it.

lines.japanese: 「……んあー？　なんか言ったー？」
lines.english: “Mmm? Did you say something?”

lines.japanese: ひとと話してる最中にメールかよ。これだから最近のガキは。最近のハゲは。
lines.english: Messaging in the middle of a conversation. Kids these days. Bald men these days.

lines.japanese: 「べつに」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 改めて言いなおすほどのことでもない。俺はベンチから立ちあがった。
lines.english: It wasn't worth restating. I rose from the bench.

lines.japanese: 「え、どこ行くの？　自分探し？」
lines.english: “What, where are you going? To find yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「いや……今日はもうソレ諦めた。しゃーねーからドカチン行ってくる」
lines.english: “No... I gave up on that for today. Guess I'll go work construction.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　それはいろいろあったんじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Huh? I thought stuff happened there.”

lines.japanese: 「いろいろあんだけども、まあ、人間稼がねーことには」
lines.english: “Various things happened, but a man still has to earn a living.”

lines.japanese: 「うんー、そだねー。がんばりー」
lines.english: “Yeah, true. Do your best.”

lines.japanese: 「どーも」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: こんな小娘に励まされてる。俺もいよいよだ。
lines.english: Reduced to being encouraged by a little girl. I had finally hit bottom.

lines.japanese: そのとき突然、パシャリとシャッター音が鳴った。いまどき本物のカメラじゃしない、人為的に作られたデジタルサウンド。森里が腕をまっすぐに伸ばして、携帯電話のレンズを俺へ向けていた。
lines.english: A shutter suddenly clicked. An artificial digital sound no real camera made anymore. Morisato held his arm straight out, the lens of his phone trained on me.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　んだコラ。てめ、なに撮ってんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? What the hell? Why are you taking my picture?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いちおー翔さんに写メっとこうと思って。サブジェクトは『成田発見、捕獲失敗！』みたいな」
lines.english: “Thought I'd send Kakeru a photo, just in case. Subject: ‘Narita found, capture failed!’ Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「断りなく勝手してんじゃねーよ。俺、写真嫌いなんだよ。魂とか抜かれちゃうだろ」
lines.english: “Don't do whatever you please without asking. I hate pictures. They steal your soul.”

lines.japanese: 「写真じゃねーよ。つか、ナウ撮ってるし」
lines.english: “It's not a photo. I'm shooting video now.”

lines.japanese: 「動画かよ。おー止めろテメ、どこの局だ、事務所通せコノヤロウ。蹴んぞ」
lines.english: “Video? Stop that, asshole. What station are you with? Talk to my agency. I'll kick you.”

lines.japanese: 俺はポケットに手を突っこんだまま片足を上げ、軽いミドルでカメラマンのケツを小突いた。やつはレンズを俺に向けたまま、げらげら笑って後ろへ逃げる。
lines.english: Keeping both hands in my pockets, I lifted one leg and gave the cameraman a light kick in the ass. He retreated laughing, the lens still trained on me.

lines.japanese: 「うは、こええー！　成田こええー！　おめ、少しは笑えよ、カメラ回ってんだからよー」
lines.english: “Whoa, scary! Narita is scary! Smile a little—the camera's rolling.”

lines.japanese: 「おわっち、来たッ！　カズマックス先生のグラビア撮影タイム来ましたあッ！」
lines.english: “Whoa, here it is! Kazumax glamour-shoot hour has begun!”

lines.japanese: 「は～い、イイヨイイヨ～、かわいいヨ～最高だヨ～」
lines.english: “Yeees, good, good! Adorable! Perfect!”

lines.japanese: 「こうだよ！　隼人君、こう！」
lines.english: “Like this! Hayato, like this!”

lines.japanese: 香田が手のひらをまっすぐ前に突きだして、懐かしのエッグポーズを呈示する。できるか馬鹿。
lines.english: Koda thrust one palm straight forward and demonstrated an old-school teen-magazine pose. As if I would do that, idiot.

lines.japanese: 俺はカメラ映り最悪な半開きの眼でレンズを睨んだ。この動画をご覧になるあなたへ。ありったけの想いを込めて──
lines.english: I glared into the lens through half-open eyes guaranteed to look atrocious on camera. To you, viewer of this recording, with every feeling in my heart—

lines.japanese: 「──ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “—I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「だぁーンめ、だからも、隼人君こわいってー！　普通にピースとかしてよもー」
lines.english: “Nooo! That's what I mean, Hayato, you're scary! Give us a normal peace sign!”

lines.japanese: 「っせーな、グラドルに向かって怖いとか言うな」
lines.english: “Shut up. Don't tell a pinup model she looks scary.”

lines.japanese: 仕方なく俺は言われたとおりにＶサインを作った……が、すぐに馬鹿らしくなり、それを手首から前に倒して二本の指先をレンズに向けた。
lines.english: With no choice, I formed the requested V sign... but it immediately felt ridiculous, so I tipped it forward at the wrist and aimed both fingertips into the lens.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、それじゃ目潰しじゃんよ」
lines.english: “That looks like you're gouging my eyes.”

lines.japanese: 「いちいちうっせえな、いいんだよ、目潰しピースっつんだよコレ。言っとくけど流行んぞコレ。じき時代来っかんな。修学旅行の集合写真とか、みんな真似しまくりだかんな」
lines.english: “Quit complaining. It's fine. This is the Eye-Gouging Peace Sign. I'm telling you now, it'll catch on. Its time is coming. Before long, everybody will copy it in school-trip group pictures.”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃはは、そんな糞だっせーの何年待っても来ねッて！　隼人先輩そんな恥ずかしいのより、コレやってよコレ。コレかっけーんだよマジ、皇帝自ら考案のＹＦＢ公式ハンドサインで──」
lines.english: “Gya-ha-ha, that looks like absolute shit! Wait a hundred years and it still won't catch on! Hayato, forget that embarrassment and do this. This one's seriously cool—the official YFB hand sign designed by the Emperor himself—”

lines.japanese: 「やんねえよ」
lines.english: “Not doing it.”

lines.japanese: <12>\「──ひぎい！　目があああ！」
lines.english: “—Agh! My eyes!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ソレいいかも！　隼人君ソレこっち、そのままこっち、目線ちょーだい！」
lines.english: “Oh, that might be good! Hayato, hold it right there—now look this way! Eyes on me!”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「はいフリーズ！　そこで一言、心あたたまるメッセージを、どうぞ！」
lines.english: “Freeze! And now, one heartwarming message. Go!”

lines.japanese: 「心あたたまるメッセージ」
lines.english: “A heartwarming message.”

lines.japanese: そう言われてふと俺の頭に浮かんだ選択肢は、いつもの「ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」ともうひとつ。
lines.english: At the prompt, two choices came to mind: my customary *I'll fucking kill you, asshole*, and one other.

lines.japanese: それは昔、近所のじいさんが口癖みたいに唱えていたフレーズ。
lines.english: It was a phrase an old man in my neighborhood used to recite like a personal refrain.

lines.japanese: 俺は急に懐かしくなってそっちを選んだ。
lines.english: A sudden nostalgia made me choose that one.

lines.japanese: カメラ目線で目潰しピース、アンド心あたたまるメッセージ。
lines.english: Eye-Gouging Peace Sign to the camera, plus one heartwarming message.

lines.japanese: 「世界が平和でありますように」
lines.english: “*May peace prevail on Earth*.”

lines.japanese: おまえ、マジ流行んぞコレ。
lines.english: I'm serious. This is going to catch on.
